summary: Set 114 S1 made posting the step checklist observable and then enforced it. Rendering the checklist is now what records it: every CLI render appends one line to checklist-posts.jsonl (session, timestamp, step count, which step carried the here-marker), and the new checklist_posted close gate compares that ledger against the transitions the session's own records already show - startedAt in session-state.json, each test-runs.jsonl record, each completed round in sN-rounds.jsonl, each human-authority row in decisions.jsonl, and the newest activity-log.json entry. One post per transition, consumed in time order, so a single post at the end cannot cover a whole session. A sibling ledger rather than a new activity-log entry kind, because an entry would be rendered by the checklist itself and would satisfy the existing activity_log_entry gate for a session that logged no real step. The ledger is freshness-exempt (a post after a stamped round would otherwise stale it and buy a fresh metered backstop round, making posting cost money and guaranteeing the obligation decays again) but evidence-visible (hiding it from the verifier would be a self-authorized reduction in verifier visibility). The cadence is defined in session-constitution.md Step 4 and the authoring guide, whose table marks each moment gate-checked or not: the two before-X moments cannot be checked because every record this framework keeps is written after the thing it describes, and a declared one would be the self-attestation the spec's Decision 3 forbids. That residual was disputed by the verifier and settled by operator adjudication. Four verification rounds; five of six blocking findings fixed, the sixth adjudicated. 3693 pytest passed, 33 Playwright passed.

reason.specifics: Session 2 reverses a recorded design decision (Set 111 S4's render-the-record-never-synthesize-the-plan) in the one way that decision's own reasoning permits - by writing the plan into the record at start_session. That is a continuation of the argument this session made about where a record belongs and what a renderer may invent, not a fresh problem. Full reasoning, and the three things S2 must not inherit uncritically, are in ai-assignment.md.

checklist.attestation: Operator adjudication, 2026-08-09: the checklist_posted gate this session ships correctly refused this session -- no post was recorded after verification round 2 (18:34) or round 4 (19:58). Both are genuine cadence misses by the orchestrator, and the ledger shows them. A closed window cannot be re-entered, and the only other exit was --force, which bypasses every other gate; the operator chose to add the attested-waiver escape and waive these two posts with the omission left on the record.
